issues.description: The template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java does not declare the expected class Farm as specified in the problem statement and shown in the solution. Instead it contains a malformed/duplicated declaration of class AnimalFarm with broken contents. This conflicts with the problem UML and the solution (which provide a public class Farm) and will prevent students from compiling and implementing the Farm class or following instructions (Main.java instantiates Farm).
issues.suggestedFix: Replace or fix src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java in the template so it declares a public class named Farm (not AnimalFarm) with the expected structure and stubs (List<Animal> animals, constructor initializing the ArrayList, getter/setter for animals, addAnimal(Animal), feedAllAnimals(), singFarmSong(), and a private singFarmSongVerse(Animal)). Remove duplicated/malformed code and ensure the filename matches the class name so Main.java can instantiate Farm and students can implement the intended design.

issues.description: The template file declares the core farm class as 'AnimalFarm' while the problem statement and the solution use 'Farm'. This mismatch (file named Farm.java but class named AnimalFarm) breaks the expected mapping between the assignment description and the starter code, likely causing students to search for or implement the wrong class name and preventing tests that expect class Farm from finding it.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in the template to 'Farm' (public class Farm) so it matches the problem statement and the solution. Ensure the class name matches the filename Farm.java and update any internal references accordingly.
